paper.title_en: Development of a magnetic field monitoring system for the MAGIS-100 experiment
paper.abstract_en: The MAGIS-100 collaboration is building a long-baseline atom interferometer designed to investigate dark matter, novel forces, gravitational waves, and quantum science. A major design challenge is external, time-varying magnetic fields, the effect of which can mimic gravitational waves or expected dark matter signals; static magnetic fields must also be tightly controlled to manage measurement resolution. Several tools are being applied to the problem, including mu-metal shielding, field biasing, and a suite of magnetometers. This report details the development of a magnetic field monitoring system to be built from commercially available parts and installed at seventeen locations, one for each of the modular sections making up the length of the MAGIS-100 apparatus.
